gen-gf-tektur-gf-headland-one: Expressive and a bit odd, Tektur draws pipe-cleaner strokes with open curve endings. Headland One follows with gentle thick-thin modulation and widely spaced serif letters, smooth enough that a long passage glides along.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-hedvig-letters-serif: Marker-plain and quirky up top, with Tektur's outsized lowercase. Hedvig Letters Serif sits below with a sturdy, tall body and modest thick-thin contrast, so a longer stretch of text reads like a classic serif should.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa is a classic serif with tall, sturdy lowercase and soft contrast in every curve. Lisu Bosa does the quiet text work, while Tektur is the one for pipe-like, constant-width display lettering.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-marcellus-sc: Drafting-pen outlines, all one nib width. Marcellus SC sits underneath with mild but visible contrast and pulled-back terminals, a text serif with the stature of cast iron capitals, which gives the pair its weight.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-montagu-slab: Tektur leads with generous openings on every curve, a single thread of stroke that your eye follows easily. And Montagu Slab, a classic serif with a sizable x-height, carries a longer stretch of text with sturdy downstrokes and slender turns.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Pipe-bodied and distinctive, Tektur takes the top spot with open curves. Noto Serif Hentaigana, a classic serif, adds low-key thick-thin variation and small letters nearly as tall as capitals, so the two sit together on the page with a clear change of pace.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-bespoke-slab: Commanding is how Tilt Neon looks, with tube-like outlines drawn in one width. But Bespoke Slab, a classic serif with tall lowercase bodies, does the grounded, refined reading work that outlines like those can't.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-erode: Tilt Neon brings a splayed c and tube-like strokes. Erode, a serif with thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, gives that bold, uniform lettering a dignified editorial partner on the page.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads as a classic serif with barely any gap between x-height and caps, giving it a dense, refined look. Trench Slab against Tilt Neon's tube-like thickness, which holds through every bend, is where the pair is strongest.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-domine: Dignified in tone, Domine is a classic serif with compact ascenders and breathing space inside every curve, while Tilt Neon squeezes out its stroke like toothpaste in one line. Tilt Neon is best at bold display, Domine at refined text.
